note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see docs/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 revenue guide of $219-221m is flat sequentially on Q1's $220m, but the company's only observable prior year grew +9.6% sequentially over the same fiscal quarters (Q1 FY26 $157.1m -> Q2 FY26 $172.2m, derivable from the disclosed 9M FY26 revenue of $524.3m less Q3 FY26 of $195m, and cross-checked by the stated 40% and 28% YoY growth rates); consensus of $220.5m is the guide midpoint to within $0.5m, so the street has not applied that seasonality at all.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is in a press release. Q1 FY27 revenue $220.23m and the Q2 guide of $219-221m/28% are in the 2026-06-10 release; Q1 FY26 $157.5m is the stated comparative in that same release; Q3 FY26 $195m and 9M FY26 $524m are in the 2025-12-15 release, so Q2 FY26 of ~$171.5m is a single subtraction from two wire-distributed documents (the hunter's $172.2m and +9.6% are slightly off; true is $171.5m and +8.9%). More damaging, management pre-empted the inference on the Q1 call: Navan guided to a 'seasonally slightly weaker summer season', a phrase that was carried into the wire summaries of the guide (MarketScreener, 2026-06-10). So the street has not 'failed to apply seasonality' — it applied the seasonality management supplied. And the conclusion the finding is really making, that the guide is sandbagged and Navan beats, is the explicitly published sell-side call: Oppenheimer on 2026-08-27 named the very consensus figures ($220.5m revenue, $2.86bn bookings) and said it expects Navan to exceed both, lifting its target to $35; BofA went to $34 from $26 in early September. The market has also watched this company beat its own guide midpoint by ~10% ($161-163m guided, $178m printed for Q4 FY26) and gap +43%, then beat and raise and gap +8.4%. A serial sandbagger sandbagging is structural, not news. What is left unpriced is only the specific quantified sequential comparison — nobody I found has written 'flat vs +9% last year' — which is worth something but not much against 110% ATM IV and a 14% implied move.

findings.finding: The price half of Navan's gross bookings accelerated sharply across its fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026): US CPI airline fares ran +26.7%, +26.5% and +25.5% YoY in May/Jun/Jul against +7.1%, +14.9% and +20.7% in Feb/Mar/Apr, its fiscal Q1 -- roughly a 12pp step-up -- while consensus gross bookings of $2.86bn implies a 7.7% sequential DECLINE from Q1's $3.1bn, versus a roughly +1% sequential move in the same fiscal quarters a year earlier.
findings.adversary_note: The macro input is about as public as a number can be: BLS CPI is a scheduled monthly release with universal wire coverage, the July print landed on 2026-08-12 with airline fares +25.5% y/y called out, and dedicated trackers (usinflationcalculator's airfare page, NerdWallet's monthly travel inflation report) publish the series continuously. It is also already connected to Navan in print — Navan itself published its Business Travel Benchmark on 2026-07-14, covered by Business Travel News, BTN Europe and TravelMole, showing H1 2026 platform fares up 14.4% domestic and 9.1% international with spend +21.5% on 8.8% higher volume. That is Navan's own realised fare inflation and it is roughly half the CPI print, which is the honest rebuttal to the magnitude: leisure-weighted, US-only, hedonically adjusted CPI is not the pass-through Navan books. Management put a number on the channel — 3pp of 50pp of Q1 bookings growth from travel inflation — so a 12pp CPI step-up is worth low single digits of bookings growth, not 12. Oppenheimer's 2026-08-27 note explicitly cites 'a solid corporate travel environment' and supportive travel-supplier earnings as its reason to expect a bookings beat against the very $2.86bn the finding calls unchallenged. What survives: the specific observation that $2.86bn is a -7.7% sequential against +1% in the same fiscal quarters last year is arithmetic I could not find published anywhere, and it does check out against the disclosed FY26 GBV of $9.1bn.

findings.finding: The 12% drawdown from the 2026-08-27 all-time high is at least partly mechanical post-lock-up insider supply, not a fundamental de-rating: CEO Ariel Cohen sold 168,378 shares directly plus 75,000 through each of three GST trusts at $30.1441 on 08-27 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06, alongside a cluster of five Form 4s filed 08-24 and four Form 144s filed 08-27.
findings.adversary_note: This claim asks to reinterpret a price move that has already fully happened, using filings that are already published and syndicated. The Form 4s are on EDGAR and are picked up by StockTitan's NAVN filings feed and Investing.com's insider-trading desk, which has covered Cohen's sales before; the 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06 is disclosed in Navan's own periodic Rule 408 disclosure, including its 225,000-share Class A cap — which is exactly the 3 x 75,000 the trusts sold, i.e. the plan simply ran out. The drawdown itself is in the sealed baseline (run_up_20d -7.19%, -12.2% from the 52-week high) and is therefore in the price by construction. The causal mechanism is the weak part and I think it is wrong: 393,378 shares is roughly $11.9m against 20-day average volume of 2.16m shares, about 18% of one session, and it printed on 2026-08-27 — the day of the $30.58 all-time high close, not during the decline that followed. A far better-supported account of that day is Oppenheimer's target raise to $35, published the same day, producing a spike and fade, followed by de-risking into a print carrying a 14% implied move on a stock ten months from IPO. Calling a nine-session, twelve-percent drawdown 'mechanical' on the basis of a completed one-day sale is not a mechanism that reaches.

findings.finding: US airline-fare CPI averaged +26.2% y/y across May-July 2026 (Navan's fiscal Q2) versus +14.2% y/y across Feb-April 2026 (fiscal Q1), and the seasonally-adjusted index rose 6.4% sequentially between those two windows (291.3 avg to 310.0 avg) — a ~12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind to gross booking volume inside the quarter management guided to 28% revenue growth, down 12pp from Q1's 40%.
findings.adversary_note: Structurally the same claim as h1#1 with better index construction (the seasonally-adjusted 291.3 to 310.0 sequential move is a nicer statistic than the y/y pairs, and I found it published nowhere), but with no company-specific arithmetic at all — it is a wire-level macro series set against a wire-level guidance number. Both halves are fully published: the BLS release of 2026-08-12 and the $219-221m/28% guide of 2026-06-10. The bridging mechanism is where it fails to reach: management already told the market on that same call that travel inflation contributed 3pp of 50pp of bookings growth and that it assumed 'prices being fairly stable in Q2', and Navan's own July benchmark put its platform fare inflation at 9-14%, not 26%. So the '12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind' does not convert into anything like 12pp of revenue. The deceleration from 40% to 28% that the finding treats as unexplained is also the least surprising number in the release — it is what the company guided, what the wires reported, and what an analyst asked about on the call, where the CFO answered it directly.

findings.finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 guide of $219-221m implies exactly 0% sequential revenue growth off Q1's $220m, whereas the same fiscal quarter a year earlier grew +9.1% sequentially ($157.5m to $171.9m); repeating last year's own seasonality would put Q2 at roughly $240m, i.e. +40% y/y — the same growth rate Navan just printed — against a guide of +28%.
findings.adversary_note: This is h1#0 arrived at independently, and it rests on the single most-read document in the name — the 2026-06-10 release — which is also the document that contains the rebuttal. Management characterised Q2 on that call as 'a seasonally slightly weaker summer season' and quantified the price channel at only 3pp of the 50pp Q1 gross-bookings growth, assuming 'prices being fairly stable in Q2'. The $240m extrapolation is the weakest part: it assumes FY26 seasonality repeats unchanged on a base 40% larger, with a different revenue mix (payments and subscription now growing at different rates) and a Brazilian acquisition folded in, and it sits awkwardly against a full-year guide of $907-913m that the company had just raised. As magnitude it is contested rather than established. And the trade it implies — Navan beats its guide by ~9% — is the published Oppenheimer (2026-08-27, $35 target) and BofA (early September, $34 from $26) call, on a stock the market has already watched beat its own Q4 guide by 9.9% and gap +43%.

findings.finding: CEO Ariel Cohen sold 393,378 shares at $30.1441 on 2026-08-27 — 168,378 personally plus 75,000 from each of three GST trusts, all three of which went to zero holdings — nine trading sessions before the print, and Lightspeed entities distributed roughly 2.5m shares in June at $19-20 and continued trimming in July.
findings.adversary_note: The same accession as h1#2, read the opposite way, and the reading does not survive the filing itself. The sale was executed under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted on 2026-01-06 — eight months before the print and disclosed in Navan's periodic Rule 408 disclosure — which caps Class A sales at 225,000 shares, precisely the 3 x 75,000 the trusts sold. 'All three trusts went to zero' is the plan finishing on schedule, not a decision taken nine sessions before earnings, and h1#2 correctly records the plan date while this finding omits it, which is the omission that produces the bearish reading. The Lightspeed distributions of June 2026 at $19-20 are likewise routine post-IPO LP distributions, filed on Form 4 on 2026-06-23 and indexed by the same aggregators; the stock is $26.85 today, 35% above where they distributed, which is a poor advertisement for treating it as a signal. And the whole category — sponsor distribution and founder sales in a company ten months from its IPO — is the definition of structural and known. Two brokers raised targets into the same window (Oppenheimer $35 on 08-27, BofA $34 in early September); the sell-side saw the same filings and did not read them as a warning.

findings.finding: The Army's $117,306,232 firm-fixed-price order for 82 P550 UAS carries a DoD-stated estimated completion date of 2026-07-23 -- nine days inside AeroVironment's fiscal Q1 FY27, which ended 2026-08-01 -- yet consensus has Q1 product-sales revenue at $306.4M, DOWN 2.3% year over year, a number that cannot easily absorb a ~$117M program that did not exist in the year-ago quarter.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of this finding are published, and the join between them is weaker than it looks. The $117,306,232 firm-fixed-price P550 order is DoD daily-contracts wire copy: ExecutiveBiz dates the award 2026-06-03 and ClearanceJobs carried it 2026-06-04, and AeroVironment itself press-released it on 2026-07-20 with heavy re-syndication on 07-21/07-22. That award was therefore public roughly four weeks BEFORE the 2026-06-29 Q4 FY26 call at which management issued FY27 revenue guidance of $2.125-2.225B, and public again before the fiscal quarter closed on 2026-08-01. Every sell-side model built after 06-29 had the award in hand. The other half -- $306.4M product-sales consensus, -2.3% YoY -- is not a private calculation either; it is the Zacks key-metrics consensus syndicated on Yahoo Finance on 2026-09-03, six days before the print. So the only unpublished element is the inference that the two are incompatible, and that inference rests on reading a DoD 'estimated completion date' of 2026-07-23 as a revenue-recognition schedule. It is not one: it is the period-of-performance end on a BOA call order whose place of performance was explicitly 'to be determined with individual orders', and at least one secondary rendering of the same announcement gives work beginning 2026-08-03 and completing 2026-10-31, which would put the entire program in Q2 FY27 and outside this print. The more parsimonious explanation for a product line modelled down 2.3% with a known $117M order inside it is that analysts know the deliveries are not all Q1 revenue, or that Switchblade/JUMP-20 volumes are declining underneath. Finally, the baseline is already leaning this way: a 25-delta skew of -15.51 means calls are bid over puts into the print, i.e. the option market is explicitly paying for the upside surprise this finding predicts.

findings.finding: The -26.7% twenty-day drawdown is a documented sector-wide positioning unwind with explicitly no company news, layered on a mechanical share overhang: on 2026-08-24 AVAV fell 5% while RCAT -7%, ONDS -5%, UMAC -9% and KTOS -6%, with the report stating 'No company announcement, contract award, earnings release, regulatory action, or analyst rating change has been reported'; separately, 17,425,849 AVAV shares were issued to the BlueHalo seller and Arlington Capital sponsors, of which 40% (about 6.97M shares, roughly 5.6 days of the 1.25M-share ADV) came off lock-up on 2026-05-01 with a further 30% due 2026-11-01.
findings.adversary_note: The first leg restates the sealed baseline. run_up_20d_pct = -26.73 is the single most public number about this name, and a claim that the shares are down is definitionally in the price. The sector-wide framing is also published -- 24/7 Wall St. ran the same drone-complex slide story on 2026-08-18 as well as the cited 2026-08-24 piece. Worse, the finding's central assertion that there is 'no company announcement, contract award, earnings release, regulatory action, or analyst rating change' is contradicted by the record: AVAV carries a company-specific overhang from the SCAR stop-work of 2026-01-20 (a single-day -15.77% decline), the Space Force reopening SCAR to competition in March, a two-notch Raymond James cut to Underperform on 2026-03-02, and a securities class action whose lead-plaintiff notices were re-syndicated through the summer -- Quiver headlined AVAV sliding specifically on those notices, and 24/7 Wall St.'s own 2026-08-18 piece is titled 'Red Cat, Ondas Flat While AeroVironment Tumbles', which is the opposite of undifferentiated sector beta. The second leg is structural and disclosed: the 40/30/30 BlueHalo lock-up release schedule (2026-05-01, 2026-11-01, 2027-05-01) has been in the merger prospectus and the 424B3/424B5 filings since early 2025. The 40% tranche came free four months ago and is fully absorbed; the 30% tranche is due 2026-11-01, seven weeks after this print, so it cannot move tonight's tape except as a known calendar item.

findings.finding: The largest good news in this company's history is already spent and none of it is in tonight's numbers: the $464.8M E-HEL award (2026-09-02) is an Other Transaction Agreement ceiling for deliveries 'well into the dozens' spread over 'the next few years' -- a January Army draft solicitation sought up to 24 systems over five years -- it was awarded 32 days after the reported quarter ended, and AVAV gave back the entire intraday +6% pop it produced within four sessions and then failed to respond at all to the first international LOCUST order (>$50M, 2026-09-08).
findings.adversary_note: Every factual component of this is in the wire copy, and the price reaction it describes is the baseline. The E-HEL award was announced by AeroVironment itself on 2026-09-02 and covered the same day and next by DefenseScoop, Breaking Defense, Defense News and Seeking Alpha, all of which characterised it as a multiyear production contract for 'dozens' of LOCUST X3 systems -- the multiyear, ceiling-not-booked-revenue framing the finding presents as its insight is in the primary coverage. The fiscal arithmetic is not a discovery either: AeroVironment's fiscal year ends 30 April, the quarter reported tonight closed 2026-08-01, and an award dated 2026-09-02 is trivially outside it for anyone who knows the fiscal calendar. The first international LOCUST order of more than $50 million was press-released by the company on 2026-09-08 and picked up by Defense Daily, defence-blog and securities.io within hours; it is one session old and equally outside the quarter. And the fade is observable rather than inferred: run_up_5d_pct is -0.38%, so the shares sit flat against the 2026-09-02 close, having produced no follow-through from either announcement. A finding whose evidence is that the market did not stay excited is a finding agreeing with the market. The one genuinely obscure element is the January Army draft solicitation seeking up to 24 systems over five years, which sizes the ceiling against realistic annual deliveries; that detail is not in the mainstream coverage and is worth something, but it is a valuation argument about FY28-FY30, not about tonight's reaction.

findings.finding: FY26 has declined at a remarkably steady rate (-11.1% Q1, -9.5% Q2, -11.6% Q3; nine months $1,210.4m, -10.3%), yet the -10%/-12% full-year guide implies Q4 revenue of $272.9m-$306.6m against a $336.6m Q4 FY25 base, i.e. -8.9% to -18.9%: simple extrapolation of the year's own run-rate lands ~$300m, at the favourable end, while a $1.50bn full-year consensus requires ~$290m (-14%), a 3-4pp step-down no quarter of FY26 has produced.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is published wire copy. The -10%/-12% FY26 revenue guide was issued with the Q3 release on 2026-05-07 and carried by Businesswire, Seeking Alpha and MSN the same day; the nine-month revenue and the Q4 FY25 base are in the same 8-K exhibit the hunter cites; and the $1.50bn full-year consensus is published on public estimate pages. The 'finding' is one subtraction on two public numbers, and it lands exactly where you would expect: $1.50bn is simply the midpoint of the company's own guide ($1.484-1.517bn), so 'consensus implies a step-down versus run-rate' is the generic arithmetic property of any guided-midpoint consensus, not a discovery about FLWS. The premise is also weaker than stated: -11.1%, -9.5%, -11.6% is not a 'remarkably steady rate', it is a re-acceleration, and Q4 (Apr-Jun) is the Mother's Day quarter where the Consumer Floral segment that fell 18.7% in Q3 carries the heaviest mix weight — which is a reason the favourable end of the guide is the less likely end, not the more likely one. Finally the mechanism is thin for this name: the last two prints moved +16.5% and +14.6% on a large revenue miss with a $45.2m impairment and on holiday-quarter results, so a $10m revenue delta against a $228m market cap is not what sets the tape here.

findings.finding: The short base has not moved all year while the ability to exit has collapsed: short interest was 8,419,051 shares (27.5% of float) on 30 April 2026 and 7,754,157 (25.3%) on 14 August 2026, but days-to-cover went from 4.33 to 48.96 as average volume fell to ~200k/day, and the option chain offers no exit either (6,544 contracts total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM bid-ask 67% of mid).
findings.adversary_note: 'FLWS is a heavily shorted squeeze candidate' is one of the most widely republished facts about this ticker. Fintel, shortsqueeze.com, Benzinga and MarketBeat all carry dedicated FLWS short-interest and short-squeeze-score pages, FINRA publishes the underlying number twice a month, and the stock has already been swept into a meme-stock rally on exactly this basis. Two of the last three prints produced +16.5% and +14.6% one-day moves — the squeeze-on-print dynamic is not a hypothesis, it is the observed reaction history sitting in the sealed baseline. Worse, three of the four numbers in the finding's second clause (6,544 total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM spread 67% of mid) are copied verbatim from the sealed baseline's own options block, so they are by construction not new information, and the low average volume (199,621) is likewise a sealed-baseline field. The one genuinely new-looking claim is the 4.33 -> 48.96 days-to-cover jump, and it does not survive its own source: the MarketBeat series the hunter cites reads 25.88 (3/13), 33.04 (4/15), 4.33 (4/30), 7.52 (5/15), 22.75 (6/15), 36.35 (7/15), 30.67 (7/31), 48.96 (8/14). 4.33 is the single lowest reading in the series, chosen as the base. And 'the short base has not moved all year' is contradicted on the same page: shares short fell from 9,299,354 (3/13) to 7,754,157 (8/14), a 17% reduction — shorts have been covering steadily, not standing still.

findings.finding: At the identical print one year ago the company explicitly declined to give numerical FY2026 guidance, framing the year instead as 'a pivotal period of foundation setting', and on the May 2026 call management again declined to provide any FY2027 numbers while noting the $12-13m of consultant costs expire 30 June.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of this are public documents that anyone covering the name has read. The 2025-09-04 press release — a Businesswire item and an 8-K exhibit — is where the 'pivotal period of foundation setting' framing and the absence of numerical FY26 guidance appear, and I confirmed by fetching it that it gives strategic priorities and no numbers. The May 2026 call, at which management gave no FY27 figures and flagged the $12-13m of consultant costs rolling off 30 June, is published in full transcript on Motley Fool, Investing.com and The Globe and Mail. So the observation is: a company that did not guide last September and did not guide in May is unlikely to guide this September. That is the default expectation, not a variant one. Crucially, the outcome of the exact event this finding describes is already in the sealed baseline: the 2025-09-04 no-guidance print moved the stock -2.81%, comfortably inside the 5.75% deadband. The market has seen this movie and priced it as a non-event. The finding also has no clean sign — absence of a FY27 guide can read as persistent uncertainty (negative) or as removing a disappointing number from the tape (positive) — and a finding whose direction is ambiguous cannot carry much of a ranking.

findings.finding: The May 2025 credit-agreement amendment that replaced the leverage and fixed-charge tests with a minimum-liquidity covenant runs out at the fiscal quarter ending 27 December 2026, at which point the ratio covenants snap back, and the same amendment cut revolver commitments to $205m with a seasonal reduction to $125m — or $50m during the 'Affected Period' — from 1 January to 1 July each year; the FY26 10-K filed with this print has to speak to compliance across that snapback.
findings.adversary_note: The Second Amendment has been on the tape since 2025-05-07 in an 8-K, and has been restated in the FY25 10-K filed 2025-09-05 and in each of the three FY26 10-Qs, most recently the Q3 10-Q filed 2026-05-07 which states the company was in compliance with the minimum-liquidity covenant as of 29 March 2026 with $50.7m of cash and $94.3m of net debt. This is a primary document that every analyst on a 3-analyst small cap has read four times. More damagingly, the 8-K itself undercuts the risk the finding implies: the same amendment that installed the liquidity covenant also *decreased* the minimum fixed-charge coverage ratio and *increased* the maximum leverage ratio for the period running through the fiscal quarter ending 28 March 2027. So what snaps back on 27 December 2026 is not the original ratio test but a deliberately loosened one — the amendment was engineered as a glide path, not a cliff, and the finding presents it as the latter. The revolver step-down to $125m (or $50m in the Affected Period) between 1 January and 1 July is likewise a seasonal facility sizing disclosed sixteen months ago and already lived through once in FY26 without incident. The residual live question — whether the FY26 10-K's going-concern look-forward window, which now spans the snapback, carries new language — is real, but it was equally true of last year's 10-K (whose window ran past September 2026) and produced nothing.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26 laps the second-weakest lemon price in eight quarters ($17.02/carton in Q3 FY25) while management said on 9 June that realised pricing was already above $20/carton and rising about $1/carton a month, yet the 3-analyst FY26 revenue consensus of $132.13M against $42.1M of actual H1 revenue implies H2 of ~$90.0M versus H2 FY25's $90.3M - i.e. the sell side is modelling H2 flat and giving no credit to either the price comp or the Sunkist volume shift into H2.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is wire copy. The $17.02/carton Q3 FY25 comp was in the September 2025 release; the '$20+/carton and about $1/carton a month between now and October' quote is in the 9 June call transcript and was picked up in the reporting summaries ('buoyed by lemon prices exceeding $20 per carton'); and the Sunkist volume shift into H2 is not an inference at all - the 9 June press release states in terms that the company expects H2 to be its seasonally strongest period with Q3/Q4 benefiting from higher lemon volumes under the Sunkist agreement. What is genuinely new is only the subtraction ($132.13M less $42.1M = $90.0M against H2 FY25's $90.3M), which is mechanical and rests on a three-analyst S&P Global consensus that is a weak statement of what a $270M microcap's marginal holder expects. The tape suggests the market has already credited the recovery: the stock is 17% above the $12.85 of the 2 June Groundbreaker thesis, +7.65% over 20 days and only 4.26% off its 52-week high, with call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.67). The finding also omits the half of the comp that cuts the other way - Q4 FY25 realised $23.33/carton, above management's current $20+, so the favourable price lap exists in Q3 and reverses in Q4, which is exactly why a flat H2 consensus is defensible rather than lazy.

findings.finding: The reiterated FY26 guide of 4.0-4.5M fresh lemon cartons is arithmetically stretched: H1 FY26 delivered 681,000 (Q1, $17.41) + 1,028,000 (Q2, $16.63) = 1,709,000 cartons, down ~32% year on year, so the guide requires H2 of 2,291,000-2,791,000 against H2 FY25's 1,397,000 + 821,000 = 2,218,000 - the top end would need a Q4 (Aug-Oct, the seasonal trough) of roughly 1.9M cartons versus 821,000 last year, which the company has never done.
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is right but the framing overstates it, and every number in it is in the wire copy of two press releases. The 4.0-4.5M carton guide and the 681,000 / 1,028,000 H1 splits are in the Q1 and Q2 FY26 releases; the 1,397,000 and 821,000 H2 FY25 comparatives are in the Q3 and Q4 FY25 releases. Subtracting H1 from a reiterated full-year guide is the first thing any of the three covering models does. More damaging: the low end of the range needs H2 of 2,291,000 against 2,218,000 last year - up 3.3%, which is precisely the modest step-up management attributed to the Sunkist cadence shift. Only the 4.5M top end requires the ~1.9M Q4 the finding calls impossible, and guiding to a range whose top is a stretch is not a surprise, it is what a range is for. On a name where the last four prints moved on impairments, asset sales and EBITDA, printing 4.1M instead of 4.5M cartons is not the swing factor. And this is the number that gets published tonight - reading it off the guide two hours early is not an edge over the tape.

findings.finding: Limoneira's lender deferred the debt service coverage ratio covenant in December 2025 so that it next resumes 'measurement as of October 31, 2026' at 1.25:1.0 - six weeks after the fiscal year the company is now two-thirds through - against H1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of minus $9.4M (Q1 -$7.7M, Q2 -$1.7M), FY25 full-year adjusted EBITDA of minus $6.452M, total debt of $94,120,000, cash of $891,000 and only $22,096,000 of remaining revolver capacity.
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing sentence is misread, and the misreading inverts it. The December 2025 amendment does not make the covenant resume at 31 October 2026 - it defers the 31 October 2026 measurement. The 10-Q language is 'defer measurement as of October 31, 2026 and resume a debt service coverage ratio of 1.25:1.0 measured as of October 31, 2027 and for any fiscal year ending thereafter', and the underlying 8-K exhibit 10.1 states the minimum DSCR as 'greater than or equal to 1.25:1 for the fiscal year ending October 31, 2027'. The total net leverage covenant is likewise deferred through 31 July 2027. So there is no test six weeks after this fiscal year end; the amendment removed exactly the risk the finding describes, and it did so nine months ago. Everything else in the finding - H1 adjusted EBITDA of about -$9.5M, total debt $94.1M, cash $891k, revolver headroom - is in the 9 June 10-Q and release and was covered the same day (TipRanks, 'Limoneira Bets on Asset Monetization After Tough Quarter'), and the covenant was already singled out as 'the near-term constraint' in a public 2 June thesis piece. Since then the position has improved in public: Windfall Farms was auctioned on 17 August for $15M all cash closing 14 September, against the $10M cash plus $6M seller note management had guided on the June call.

findings.finding: The federal gate for Limoneira's stated FY2026 Colorado River water monetisation opened 19 days before this print: Interior issued the post-2026 Record of Decision on 21 August 2026, ordering 1.25 million acre-feet of annual Lower Basin reductions with Arizona absorbing 760,000 acre-feet - and Limoneira decided in April 2026 to cease citrus farming on its last 600 lemon acres in Yuma specifically 'to monetize Class 3 Colorado River water rights by conserving water', telling investors it expects a monetisation event in fiscal 2026 (which ends 31 October).
findings.adversary_note: Both halves are published; only the join is not. The Interior Record of Decision of 21 August was a heavily covered national story - Navajo Times, azfamily, KNAU, Western Water all carried the 1.25 maf Lower Basin cut and Arizona's 760,000 acre-feet on the day - so it is not an obscure document. And the Limoneira side is squarely in the wire copy: the April 2026 decision to cease citrus on the last 600 Yuma acres 'to monetize Class 3 Colorado River water rights by conserving water', the 9 June release's statement that the company 'anticipates a monetization event from its Colorado River water rights in fiscal year 2026', and the CFO's call comment naming the 31 December 2026 contract expiries as the trigger. A public long thesis on 2 June had already valued the water at $50-70M of catalyst. The dated catalyst was therefore in investors' hands three months before the ROD. Two further discounts: the ROD's mandatory Arizona reduction falls overwhelmingly on priority-4 CAP rather than on priority-3 on-river districts like Yuma Mesa, so the paying channel is the voluntary 700,000 acre-feet conservation tranche rather than the mandatory cut - 'the gate opened' is softer than stated; and the ROD changes nothing in the May-July quarter being reported, so it reaches tonight only as call commentary. Against that, I concede the specific join - that the federal precondition for the company's own stated FY26 monetisation cleared 19 days before this print - appears nowhere I could find, and no 8-K has announced a Colorado River deal (the only monetisation press release, $30,000/acre-foot, was Santa Paula Basin in January 2025). That is why this is the least-priced of the four.

findings.finding: FY27 guidance requires a four-point inflection in the revenue trend starting in the quarter being reported: FY26 total revenue was $512.7m less $108.9m of Global Knowledge equals ~$403.8m of continuing (TDS) revenue, so the $388-406m FY27 guide brackets flat; Q1 FY27 was $94.5m, -4.7% YoY, which leaves the guide midpoint needing Q2-Q4 at about -0.7% versus a Q1 running at -4.7% and a company that itself flagged 'softness in government bookings' and consumer down 21%.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this arithmetic is published and none of it is obscure. The $388-406m FY27 range is not a June disclosure at all -- it was set on 2026-04-07 as an explicit TDS-only outlook against FY26 TDS revenue of $403.7m stated in the same 8-K, so 'the guide brackets flat on continuing revenue' was on the tape the day it was issued and the stock fell 12.02% that day. Q1 at $94.5m / -4.7%, the government-bookings softness and the 21% consumer decline are all in the 2026-06-09 release and call, on which the stock fell 13.70%. The $108.9m / $512.7m / $403.7m pro-forma bridge is in the 2026-07-10 exhibit the hunter cites. Third parties have already published a full-year revenue model: S&P's 2026-08-12 downgrade note projects 'fiscal 2027 revenues near $400 million', i.e. exactly the guide midpoint, and the quoted Q2 consensus of $99.0m against a Q2 FY26 TDS base of $101m already embeds ~2.7 of the claimed 4 points of inflection. Management also publicly pre-explained the back-half shape on 2026-06-09 (labour-based professional-services and coaching revenue 'shifting to periods later in this fiscal year', FCF resuming in Q4), so the required trajectory is stated guidance, not a hidden implication. What is genuinely undrawn is only the crisp subtraction that Q2-Q4 must run -0.7% against a Q1 running -4.7%; I could find no article stating that number. That residual, plus the fact that the recent 29% drawdown is traceable to credit rather than to revenue trend, is why this is not in the 80s.

findings.finding: Q2 FY27 (May 1 - Jul 31, 2026) is new CFO Ron Kisling's first full quarter — he started 2026-05-20, twenty days before the June 9 reaffirmation — and his predecessor John Frederick's transition-advisory contract expired 2026-09-04, five days before this print, so the first quarter he can fully own is the first one reported without the author of the inherited guidance still under contract.
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing facts are both published and one of them is wire-level: Kisling's appointment effective 2026-05-20 and Frederick's retirement were announced in an 8-K filed 2026-05-21, and Kisling was already on the 2026-06-09 call speaking to the reaffirmed guidance. The 'new CFO's first owned quarter, therefore reset risk' heuristic is one of the most widely rehearsed setups in earnings analysis and is age, not novelty. What the hunter adds is the Frederick advisory-expiry date of 2026-09-04, which is genuinely obscure -- it is a clause in the 2026-05-21 8-K body and I found no article, note or screen that connects it to tonight's print -- so this is not a high number. But obscurity is doing all the work: the mechanism is weak. A retiring CFO's advisory contract lapsing on a routine ~3.5-month schedule confers no authority over guidance and did not restrain Kisling on 2026-06-09, when he had been in the chair twenty days and reaffirmed the range anyway. The date coincidence is decorative; the real content is the generic reset-risk trope, and that is thoroughly known. Note too that Kisling co-owns the guide already, having publicly reaffirmed it, which cuts directly against the clean-slate framing.

findings.finding: The two enterprise-learning comps that reported after Skillsoft last spoke on June 9 disagree with each other, and the closer pure-play comp is the positive one: Docebo (2026-08-07) reported ARR +9.5% YoY, a second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, and RAISED full-year revenue guidance by $3.5m citing enterprise strength, while Coursera (2026-07-29) reported enterprise NRR down to 91% on L&D budget pressure.
findings.adversary_note: Both legs are ordinary, heavily covered public earnings events from listed companies with real analyst followings, reported on their scheduled dates and picked up across Investing.com, GuruFocus, Yahoo and the wires within hours. Docebo's 2026-08-07 print -- ARR $255.1m, +9.5% YoY, second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, FY guidance lifted $3.5m -- was covered as a beat-and-raise with a transcript headline reading 'lifts outlook'; Coursera's 2026-07-29 enterprise NRR was reported the same way. Nothing here is unpublished; the only step the hunter takes is the read-across to Skillsoft, which is the standard sector exercise any generalist performs and which multiple outlets already frame as 'enterprise L&D demand'. It is also self-cancelling on its own terms: the finding states the two comps disagree, then privileges the favourable one on a similarity judgement that is contestable -- Docebo is a mid-market LMS platform re-accelerating partly on acquisitions and an OEM base, while Skillsoft's decline is driven by government contract losses absorbed over a 12-15 month cycle and a 21% consumer decline, neither of which Docebo has any exposure to. A read-across whose direction depends on which comp you choose is not information.

findings.finding: Tonight is the first call at which a refinancing update is contractually due: on 2026-06-09 Hovsepian said addressing the debt maturities becomes 'management's top financial priority' once the Global Knowledge sale closes, and it closed 2026-07-06 — a $574.6m term loan due 2028-07-16 against $115.6m cash and a ~$60m equity, so any constructive statement is worth far more in percentage terms than silence costs.
findings.adversary_note: The refinancing question is not merely known here, it is the dominant published narrative on this name and it demonstrably moved the price inside the very drawdown the brief asks me to account for. On 2026-08-12 S&P downgraded Skillsoft to 'CCC+' from 'B-' with a negative outlook, explicitly on 'high leverage and refinancing risk ahead of the company's 2028 debt maturity', publishing the liquidity numbers ($115m cash, $75m AR facility), the ~7x leverage path, and the warning that it could cut further if the potential for a distressed transaction rises. That is the single largest published event in the 20-session window and gives the -29% a specific, refinancing-shaped cause. Upstream of it, Hovsepian's 'top management priority' language and Kisling's 'addressing our upcoming debt maturities' are both in the 2026-06-09 transcript, the Seeking Alpha wire headline for that call literally names debt refinancing, and the GK close on 2026-07-06 was filed 2026-07-10. So 'a refinancing update is due tonight and matters enormously to a $57m equity stub sitting under ~$580m of term debt' is the consensus frame, not an edge. What survives is only that the content of tonight's statement is unknown -- but that is an option-payoff assertion, not information, and the asymmetry claim is contestable in both directions: after an August downgrade that named distressed-exchange risk, silence or a hint at a liability-management exercise is not cheap, it is the outcome the credit market is already braced for. The finding's own numbers are also slightly stale: the 10-Q puts initial term loans at $580.2m at 2026-04-30, not $574.6m.

findings.finding: IFC's fund ALAC filed a fresh Form 144 on 2026-09-01 to sell a further 857,362 LSAK shares (exactly the Rule 144 1%-of-outstanding cap, ~10.3x the baseline 20-day ADV of 83,297) starting 2026-09-02 through J.P. Morgan, after selling 857,362 shares between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-07 and 808,737 shares between 2026-03-05 and 2026-04-17 — i.e. the seller was capped out and absent from the tape from 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01 and returns to it in the same week as the print.
findings.adversary_note: The document itself was picked up and written up by a retail-facing filing aggregator on the day it was filed: StockTitan's LSAK filing feed carries a 2026-09-01 headline, 'Lesaka (NASDAQ: LSAK) investor readies secondary share sale', naming IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, LP, the 857,362 shares and J.P. Morgan Securities as broker. That is not obscure — it is the same feed that covered the April 144 and the March/April/June ALAC Form 4s, so the IFC exit programme has been on the public tape continuously since at least 2026-03-04, including a 13D/A on 2026-06-17 itemising 671,112 shares sold on 22 dates. Two further points cut against the hunter's framing rather than the fact. First, 857,362 is exactly 1% of the 85,736,223 shares outstanding, i.e. the mechanical Rule 144 ceiling that essentially every affiliate files at — 'exactly the cap' is boilerplate, not a signal of urgency. Second, the baseline's own tape refutes the mechanism: the seller was, on the hunter's own reconstruction, absent from 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01, and that is precisely the window in which the stock fell (run_up_20d = -5.38%) while the 5-day run-up with the seller allegedly back on the tape is +2.24%. If the presence of ALAC drove the price, the signs are backwards. Finally the direction is ambiguous even if the supply is real: after the March-August sales ALAC's residual is roughly a million shares, so a further 857k tranche largely retires a six-month overhang, which is as easily read bullish as bearish. And a Form 144 is a supply fact, not information about tonight's numbers.

findings.finding: Nine-month FY2026 GAAP net loss attributable to Lesaka is -$461 thousand (nine months to 2026-03-31, per the company's own Q3 statement of operations), so management's repeated promise of 'the first year we will be profitable since the creation of Lesaka four years ago' rests entirely on Q4 FY26 clearing +$0.46m — in the quarter that carries the 30 June annual goodwill impairment test on R3,532,856 thousand (~$207m) of goodwill against $186.6m of total equity.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of the arithmetic are the company's own published numbers. The nine-month net loss attributable to Lesaka of $461 thousand, the R3,532,856 thousand goodwill balance and the equity figure are all in Exhibit 99.1 to the 2026-05-06 8-K, and management's FY26 positive-net-income promise is in the same release, on the 2026-05-07 call, and restated in at least four transcript outlets and in GlobeNewswire wire copy. The subtraction that turns those two published facts into 'Q4 must clear +$0.46m' is one line of arithmetic that any reader of the release can do, and management pre-announced its conclusion — they told the market the milestone would be achieved in Q4, which only makes sense if nine months were negative. The framing also overstates the fragility: Q3 itself delivered positive net income at the upper end of guidance with adjusted EBITDA +45% and adjusted EPS +247%, so a $0.46m Q4 swing is a low bar on run-rate, not a coin flip. What is genuinely undrawn is the goodwill leg — I could find no article, note or filing anywhere connecting the 30 June annual test on ~$207m of goodwill to the profitability promise, and the only prior impairment I can source is $7.0m in fiscal 2023 per the FY2024 10-K. That is a real, unpublished tail: a non-cash impairment is the one thing that could break the headline while leaving guidance-basis EBITDA intact. But it is also a generic risk-factor item disclosed in every 10-K, there is no observable trigger (the stock sits +23% off its 52-week low with EBITDA compounding), and if it lands most holders will read through a non-cash charge to the adjusted numbers the company guides on. Hence mid-range rather than low: published facts, trivial arithmetic, one unpublished but low-probability tail.

findings.finding: Management pre-committed on the 2026-05-07 Q3 call that tonight's release carries FY2027 guidance plus a first-ever three-year medium-term outlook 'inclusive of Bank Zero' — but Bank Zero is still unclosed (long-stop extended 2026-06-11 from 2026-08-06 to 2027-01-31 with Prudential Authority and exchange-control consents outstanding, and no completion 8-K on EDGAR as of 2026-09-09), it issues ~12% of Lesaka's fully diluted shares plus up to R91m cash, and Lesaka's own framing is that Bank Zero only becomes profitable in the fiscal year AFTER completion.
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this claim is separately published, and three of the four are in wire or mainstream copy. The pre-commitment is a direct quote from the 2026-05-07 call — that at the September end-of-year presentation Lesaka would provide FY2027 guidance and a three-year medium-term outlook, 'inclusive of Bank Zero' given the expected completion — and it appears in the Investing.com transcript the hunter cites plus Motley Fool, Yahoo Finance, Insider Monkey and Globe and Mail write-ups of the same call. The non-completion is not obscure either: the 2026-06-11 long-stop extension from 2026-08-06 to 2027-01-31, with Prudential Authority approval outstanding, was filed as an 8-K and covered on 2026-06-17/18 by BusinessDay, TechCentral, ITWeb, MyBroadband, BusinessTech, The Citizen, Globe and Mail and StockTitan. The ~12% fully diluted issuance plus up to R91m cash has been in the deal's public description since the 2025-06-27 announcement, and 'Bank Zero turns profitable the year after completion' is management's own published framing. So the only thing the hunter adds is the join — that a guidance package promised 'inclusive of Bank Zero' now has to be delivered with the deal unclosed — and that join is available to any reader who saw both June headlines. It is also directionally two-sided: a first-ever three-year outlook is as plausibly a positive catalyst as a disappointment, and the fact that no completion 8-K exists is a negative-space observation the market already made when the long-stop moved. I searched the JSE/SENS route as well and found no August 2026 announcement; the most recent SENS item I can source is the 2026-05-18 headline-earnings correction, so nothing there is unpublished either.

findings.finding: Kewaunee ran a book-to-bill of roughly 0.83 for all of FY26 -- consolidated backlog fell $214.6m -> $205.0m -> $192.9m -> $183.2m -> $165.9m across five straight quarters (an accelerating burn, -$17.3m in Q4 alone) while quarterly revenue was held flat at $71.1m / $70.1m / $69.4m / $71.4m -- and the FY26 10-K states 'not less than 90% of our order backlog at April 30, 2026 will be shipped during fiscal year 2027', i.e. >=$149m of shipments from backlog against $282m of FY26 revenue; with FY26 opex of $63.7m (~$15.9m/quarter, largely fixed) and a 28.5% gross margin, breakeven revenue is ~$56m per quarter, so Q1 FY27 revenue anywhere in the $55-63m range against the $71.1m year-ago comp puts EPS near zero versus $1.04.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this finding was published, and the conclusion was published too. The 2026-06-23 Q4/FY26 8-K release gave backlog of $165.9m (LPG $118.8m, International $47.1m) against $214.6m a year earlier; the FY26 10-K of 2026-06-26 carries the '>=90% shipped during fiscal 2027' line; the quarterly revenue strip ($71.1m/$70.1m/$69.4m/$71.4m) and the $1.04 Q1 comp come straight from the four FY26 earnings releases. StockTitan headlined the 10-K 'grows sales as earnings and backlog decline' on 2026-06-26, and Seeking Alpha published the identical thesis under the title 'Backlog Suggests That A Tough Year Is Ahead' on 2026-06-27. The story was re-covered as recently as 2026-08-29. Beyond publication, the magnitude step is contested on its own terms: the $48.7m of backlog erosion is almost entirely International ($90.7m -> $47.1m, driven by completion of major projects and two cancelled India projects), while domestic Lab Products Group backlog actually rose sequentially from $114.9m at 2026-01-31 to $118.8m at 2026-04-30 -- so the 'accelerating burn' is one geography, not the franchise. And Nu Aire (closed 2024-11-01, so no comp distortion, but a biosafety-cabinet product line) is book-and-ship revenue that never sits in project backlog at all, which breaks the backlog/revenue ratio the $55-63m estimate is built on. I do concede the tape cannot refute it: at 2,073 shares a day with no call and no options, I cannot show the market set a price on any of this. That is why this is 58 and not 85.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil, the primary input to Kewaunee's steel laboratory casework and fume hoods, rose from ~$1,070/short ton at the start of Kewaunee's fiscal Q1 FY27 (SMU average, week of 2026-05-01) to $1,180/st by 2026-08-12, a four-year high with Section 232 at 50% -- a ~10% sequential input-cost step inside a quarter whose revenue is delivered against fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier.
findings.adversary_note: US hot-rolled coil is among the most heavily published prices in existence -- SMU, Fastmarkets, Nucor's posted CSP base price, and a liquid CME HRC curve all print it weekly. The hunter's move is real but understated and therefore even more conspicuous: Fastmarkets' Midwest HRC was $1,202.40 on 2026-08-20, a four-year high, against roughly $800 a year earlier, i.e. about +50% year over year rather than the +10% sequential step described. Nobody following an industrial steel fabricator can have missed a 50% input move. More damaging, Kewaunee itself published the linkage: the 2026-06-23 release names 'higher input costs, and tariff-related cost pressure' as a headwind it is managing through productivity and cost controls, and the FY26 10-K carries the standing disclosure that the company 'bear[s] the burden of possible increases in labor and material costs between quotation of an order and delivery' -- the exact fixed-price-backlog mechanism the finding claims to have found. So both the commodity and its transmission channel are on the record. What is genuinely undrawn is the quantification, and the quantification is small: on FY26 COGS of roughly $202m, steel plausibly $30-40m a year, a within-quarter purchase-price step of that size flows through with inventory lag to something on the order of $0.10-0.15 of quarterly EPS against ~$1.00. That is a rounding error next to finding #0's thesis.

findings.finding: On 2026-06-30 CEO Thomas D. Hull III settled 54,388 shares of vesting performance RSUs (which paid out at 150% of target) and elected cash settlement for 17,000 of them at $36.25 rather than taking the stock, with a further 16,243 withheld for tax -- i.e. the CEO converted roughly 60% of a large equity vest away from shares at a price essentially identical to today's $36.01.
findings.adversary_note: This one I think is close to wrong rather than merely priced, on four counts. First, publication: the Form 4 has been on EDGAR since 2026-07-02 and StockTitan has already summarised it under the headline 'Kewaunee CEO settles RSUs, uses shares for taxes,' explicitly labelling the whole transaction compensation-related -- the neutral reading is the published reading. Second, the arithmetic. The '~60% converted away from shares' figure ((17,000+16,243)/54,388 = 61%) folds mandatory tax withholding into a discretionary decision; only the 17,000 cash-settled shares were elective, 31% of the vest. And the direction of the CEO's position is the opposite of what the finding implies: pre-vest direct holdings were 33,000 shares (87,388 minus the 54,388 acquired), post-vest 54,145 -- he ended up owning 64% more stock, with zero open-market sales, plus 35,631 RSUs still outstanding. Third, the same filing records that the performance RSUs certified at 150% of target for the FY24-FY26 performance period, which is a positive statement about achieved results, not a bearish one. Fourth and decisively, the mechanism does not reach the print: a 2026-06-30 settlement date fixed by a grant agreement carries no information about revenue and margin in the May-July quarter, and $616k of cash settlement on a ~$108m market cap is immaterial either way.

findings.finding: Counter-evidence, filed deliberately because it cuts against my main finding: Avantor -- whose VWR arm is the closest public proxy for the US lab distribution channel Kewaunee sells through (two domestic dealers plus a national stocking distributor were 34% of FY26 sales) -- reported on 2026-07-29, after Kewaunee last spoke, that VWR organic growth swung from -4.8% in Q1 to +1.7% in Q2 and raised full-year guidance; Dodge's institutional planning index was also +7.8% year over year in August 2026.
findings.adversary_note: Both legs of the counter-evidence are wire copy, and both fail to reach this print. Avantor's 2026-07-29 Q2 was a major, heavily syndicated event -- VWR from -4.8% to +1.7% organic, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $0.80-0.83 from $0.77-0.83, and the stock up roughly 15% -- carried by PR Newswire, Zacks, Investing.com and Yahoo the same day. The Dodge institutional planning figure is a monthly press release from Dodge Construction Network, published 2026-09-04 for August. Neither is obscure. The read-across is the weak part in both directions: VWR is consumables distribution measured in the June quarter, whereas Kewaunee's July-quarter revenue is delivered out of fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier, so an improvement in distributor consumables demand cannot show up in tonight's revenue line. Dodge is a *planning* index that leads construction starts by roughly a year and lab furniture installs by longer still -- structurally incapable of touching a quarter that has already closed. Note also that the headline Dodge Momentum Index actually ticked *down* 0.4% in August to 282.0, with commercial planning -3.0%; the +7.8% is one sub-series selected on a year-over-year basis. I credit the hunter for filing this against their own thesis -- that is the right instinct -- but as evidence about this print it is thin.

findings.finding: Building Q2 FY27 revenue bottom-up from Wealthfront's own published monthly assets (May: cash $45.0bn / advisory $54.0bn; June: cash $44.8bn / advisory $54.3bn) at the company's own last-reported annualised take rates (cash 0.58%, advisory 0.21%) gives ~$94.5m even assuming July was flat with June, versus a sell-side consensus near $98.0m and an FY27 consensus of $384.9m that requires ~$98m in each remaining quarter.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this bottom-up has been public for two months: the May and June asset splits and net deposits were released 2026-07-07 (TPA $99.1bn, cash $44.8bn, advisory $54.3bn, cash net deposits -$235m), and the 0.58% cash / ~0.21% advisory take rates come from the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 release and call. Six to seven sell-side analysts cover the name and have been cutting continuously since the last print -- Goldman to $10.50, KBW $11.00 then $10.50, Wells Fargo $11.50 -- against a January mean target near $16. The stock at $9.655 sits below the lowest of those revised targets and 30.8% below its 52-week high, having fallen on all three prior prints. That is a market that has already stopped believing the vendor consensus line. The genuinely new part is only the *precise* size of the gap, and even that is shaky: the hunter uses 0.58% when the company disclosed a 54bp May-end run rate, so its own $94.5m is internally inconsistent with the disclosure it is built on, and I could not verify that the current Q2 revenue consensus is still $98.0m rather than already marked down. What survives is that consensus of ~$98m implies +8% QoQ off a $90.5m Q1 on roughly flat assets, which the disclosed take rates cannot produce -- that specific arithmetic I found published nowhere.

findings.finding: The mechanical driver of the cash take-rate compression — the 'Direct Deposit Plus' 25bp permanent APY uplift — launched 2026-03-02, so it was live for two of the three months of Q1 FY27 (when the cash rate fell 0.61%->0.58%) and for all three months of Q2 FY27, against a disclosed asset-weighted cross-product adoption of over 63% at June-end and rising.
findings.source_date: read live 2026-09-09; page states base 3.30% APY effective 01/30/2026 and Direct Deposit Plus +0.25% starting March 2, 2026
findings.adversary_note: The company said this itself, on the record, on 2026-06-04. The MarketBeat/TradingView summary of that call states the 58bp fee rate decline was 'driven primarily by the lower Fed funds rate and the company's new cross-product adoption incentive, which affected two months of the quarter' -- the 'two of three months' framing is management's own words, not the hunter's inference. The 25bp Direct-Deposit-Plus-Investing boost with no expiration and no balance cap is on Wealthfront's public product page, and the adoption ladder (61% at FY26 year-end, ~63% by late May) was given on the same call. The only step beyond disclosure is 'therefore three months in Q2 instead of two,' which is arithmetic anyone listening to the call performs. It also runs into a company-supplied ceiling: management put the May-end rate at 54bp but 56bp on an EFFR-neutral basis, i.e. only ~2bp of the 4bp quarterly decline is structural, which caps the incremental Q2 drag at roughly $2m of revenue -- about 2% of the quarter, not a thesis.

findings.finding: This stock's reaction function is net deposits, not EPS — the 2026-01-12 print BEAT EPS ($0.21 vs $0.20) and the stock still fell 16.8% on a $208m net deposit outflow against $874m of prior-year inflows — and cash net deposits swung from +$104m in May to -$235m in June while Wealthfront's base APY has been frozen at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 against best-in-market rates now quoted at 4.15-4.21% and Marcus at 3.50% with no strings; July and August flows are both released tonight.
findings.source_date: 2026-03-20 (page-stated); cites 2026-01-12 close $12.59, 2026-01-13 close $10.47, $208m outflow vs $874m prior-year inflow
findings.adversary_note: The two hard facts here are both public and one is in the sealed baseline. The 2026-01-12 EPS beat followed by a -16.84% reaction is in the baseline history and in public estimate tables (Q3 FY26: $0.21 actual vs $0.20 estimate, then -16.8%), and the May-to-June cash net deposit swing to -$235m was in the 2026-07-07 metrics release and was the lead of trade-press coverage ('Wealthfront hits record $99.1 billion in June as advisory inflows offset cash outflows'). That the APY has been frozen at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 is on the company's own page. The cited source is a plaintiff-firm 'securities investigation' press release, which is promotional boilerplate and adds nothing. What genuinely is not written down anywhere I found is the *reaction-function claim* -- that this stock trades on net deposits rather than EPS -- and with n=3 that is an assertion rather than a regression. The forward part (July and August cash flows both land tonight and are likely negative) duplicates WLTH-h2#4's disclosure and is the one piece with real teeth.

findings.finding: Tonight's release also carries August 2026 monthly metrics, and with the S&P 500 up 2.7% and the Nasdaq up ~4% in August, Wealthfront's $54.3bn advisory book plus ~$0.4bn of monthly advisory net deposits most likely pushes Total Platform Assets above $100bn for the first time — a round-number headline the company gets to lead with even if the July quarter-end figure is flat-to-down.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (page covers August 2026; states S&P 500 +2.7% in August after negative June and July)
findings.adversary_note: This is optics on a number the market has already been shown twice, and its arithmetic base is wrong in the direction that matters. June TPA was $99.1bn and the hunter's own cited source says the S&P was *negative in June and July* -- so the July quarter-end figure, which is the one that anchors the P&L, most likely printed below $99.1bn, and August's +2.7% is climbing back from a lower base rather than adding to $99.1bn. More damaging: the company crossed to record assets in June and the trade press led with it on 2026-07-07, and the last time record assets were reported alongside the P&L (2026-06-04, 'Record Asset Growth Amid Strategic Trade-offs') the stock fell 14.35%. A round-number headline that has demonstrably failed to hold the stock twice is not a catalyst worth more than a point or two. The August market move itself is fully public macro. The only unpriced element is that nobody has published an August TPA estimate for this specific company, which is worth something but not much.

findings.finding: Wealthfront's annualized cash management fee rate is running below its own guide and still falling — the company guided ~0.59% for fiscal Q1 2027, printed 0.58%, and the CFO disclosed on the 2026-06-04 call that the May-end rate was 54 basis points; the cause is the 'Direct Deposit + Investing' +0.25% APY boost launched 2026-03-02 which carries no expiration and no balance cap, so it compounds mechanically as asset-weighted cross-product adoption rises (61% at FY26 year-end, 62.5% at April, over 63% at June).
findings.adversary_note: Every number in this finding is company-disclosed and the hunter's own cited URL is the article that published it. The ~0.59% guide, the 0.58% print, the 54bp May-end run rate and the 56bp EFFR-neutral bridge were all given by the CFO on the 2026-06-04 call and carried in at least four syndicated summaries (MarketBeat/TradingView, GuruFocus/Yahoo, TipRanks, Benzinga transcript). The adoption ladder 61% / 62.5% / >63% is likewise disclosed. This is close to a definition of restating published guidance. It is also mildly mis-attributed: management named the lower Fed funds rate first and the incentive second, and the 56bp EFFR-neutral figure caps the structural, DD+-driven piece at about 2bp -- roughly $2m a quarter -- so the 'compounds mechanically' framing overstates a drag the company has already bounded for the market.

findings.finding: Fiscal Q2 2027 is a structurally mismatched quarter: it covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31, during which the Fed did not move (held 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29, unchanged since December 2025) so no rate benefit accrued, while Wealthfront Home Lending only launched in California and Texas on 2026-08-11 — after quarter end — meaning the full pre-launch mortgage build cost sits in Q2 with essentially zero mortgage revenue, on top of Q1 GAAP expenses already up 46% year-over-year to $75.9m against 7% revenue growth.
findings.adversary_note: This is three separately wire-reported facts stapled together. The 2026-07-29 FOMC hold at 3.50-3.75% was front-page everywhere. The Home Lending California launch on 2026-08-11 was a company press release carried by GlobeNewswire, Yahoo, National Mortgage News and the trade press. The Q1 GAAP expense figure of $75.9m, +46% YoY against 7% revenue growth, was in the 2026-06-04 release and in every call summary, and management explicitly attributed part of the gross-margin decline to home-lending startup costs -- so 'costs without revenue' is the company's own stated framing, not a discovery. The finding is also factually loose in a way that matters: Home Lending was not launching for the first time on 2026-08-11. That release describes an expansion into California on top of Colorado and Texas, with the company licensed in 28 states, so the 'full pre-launch build cost with zero mortgage revenue' premise is wrong on its face, even if mortgage revenue in the quarter is de minimis either way.

findings.finding: Schwab disclosed on 2026-08-14 that transactional sweep cash fell $8.9bn in July 2026 to $476.8bn — 1.8% of the balance in one month — 'reflecting client net purchasing activity as well as typical seasonality related to advisory fee payments', and the S&P 500 then rose 2.7% in August to record highs; at Wealthfront a dollar migrating from cash to investing loses roughly 60% of its revenue (cash fee rate ~54bp vs investment advisory running ~21bp annualised on $26.2m of quarterly revenue against ~$50bn of advisory assets), so the same client behaviour that will produce a record platform-assets headline tonight is revenue-dilutive.
findings.adversary_note: The Schwab datapoint is a monthly public release that every brokerage analyst tracks; the $8.9bn July decline to $476.8bn was reported on 2026-08-14 by Schwab, Nasdaq, StockTitan, Yahoo and the trade press, and cash sorting at Schwab is the single most-watched read-across in the sector. Schwab's own release also cuts against the extrapolation: it frames the decline as seasonal advisory-fee payments plus net purchasing, and sweep cash is still +17% YoY, while Wealthfront's cash book is -2% YoY -- these are not the same dynamic, and July at Schwab was a record core-net-new-asset month. The mix-shift arithmetic (54bp vs ~21bp, so ~60% of revenue lost per migrating dollar) is derivable directly from the 2026-06-04 disclosures and the July metrics release. What is genuinely not drawn out anywhere I found is the sign: the trade coverage of the June metrics explicitly speculated the mix shift 'may support higher-margin advisory revenue,' which is the opposite conclusion, so the dilutive read is at least contested rather than consensus.

findings.finding: The rate regime that defines this company's entire bear case has flipped: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of a 25bp HIKE, and futures price roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 2026-09-16 meeting one week after this print — while Wealthfront has held its base Cash Account APY at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 and its own 10-K states that 'in weaker macroeconomic environments with higher interest rates, our cash management products become more popular.'
findings.adversary_note: This is the most-covered macro story of the past three weeks and it is very likely already in the tape for this specific name. The three-president hawkish dissent on 2026-07-29 was reported as the first unified three-way dissent since September 2016; CNBC ran 'September Fed decision is now a coin flip as rate hike odds increase' on 2026-08-28; Yahoo ran 'FOMC September 2026 Odds for a Rate Hike Surpass 50%'; CME FedWatch was at 58.7% as of 2026-09-07. The 10-K sentence about cash products being more popular in higher-rate environments is a risk-factor boilerplate line available to anyone. And the baseline shows WLTH +8.97% over five sessions into the print against +0.57% over twenty -- a rally concentrated in exactly the window when hike odds crossed and held above 50%. Separately, the mechanism does not reach tonight's numbers at all: the 2026-09-16 meeting is a week after the print, and fiscal Q2 covers May-July, so any rate benefit lands in fiscal Q3 at the earliest and can only enter tonight through management tone.

findings.finding: Tonight is a double-disclosure event, not a normal print: because Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for the first two months of each fiscal quarter, the 2026-08-19 scheduling release states that metrics 'through August 2026' will be posted with the results — meaning July (fiscal Q2's third month) and August (fiscal Q3's first month) flows both become public for the first time tonight, alongside the P&L.
findings.adversary_note: The finding's own source is a company press release from 2026-08-19 stating in plain language that 'monthly metrics through August 2026 will be available' with the results. That is not an obscure filing detail; it was carried by GlobeNewswire, Quiver, ScanX and the usual syndication chain three weeks ago, and it describes the company's routine cadence -- the same thing happened at the 2026-06-04 print, which came with metrics through May. Nothing here is a discovery about tonight; it is a restatement of a scheduling announcement about a recurring disclosure pattern. It also carries no direction: two months of flows arriving at once raises the variance of the reaction but says nothing about its sign, which is why I size it at zero. Its only value is as scaffolding for the directional findings that name what those two months will contain.
